title: Chorus order and key changes
summary: Ridgley says everyone knew who took each chorus and varied it per piece. They did not change keys on Maryland but did on The Saints.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you have a set pattern that you would apply as to who would take the first chorus, the second chorus, the third and the fourth, to different pieces?
Yeah, always. I would have to know. You knew ahead of the time when you took on Maryland who was gonna get the solo the second
You wouldn't use the same pattern on each piece, would you? No. You'd have to vary it.
You'd have to make it. Uh-huh. Make it a little change, you know.
Would you change chords many times? Yes, sir.
No. Keys in a given piece, like they do in the Saints sometimes nowadays, you know?
We'd do it now. Oh, when in the Saints? No, we wouldn't do that in nothing like Maryland. Uh-huh. No, we didn't do that.
How about in the Saints? Would you change keys in there? We'd have to do it in there, yeah. I see.
